hero.title: Build the card sorter
hero.description: Parts list and assembly instructions for the physical sorting unit: a hopper feeds cards one at a time through {{modules}} stacked routing modules, each capable of dropping a card into one of two side bins or passing it down to the next module - {{bins}} bins total, driven by an {{board}} over I²C.
hero.modulesIntro: Each module has three servos - a <0>bottom</0> trapdoor, a <1>paddle</1> gate, and a left/right <2>pusher</2> - plus an IR sensor. Closing every trapdoor above the target bin and opening only the ones beneath it lets a card fall to the right module before the pusher ejects it.

bom.heading: Bill of materials
bom.description: Quantities scale with the number of modules you're building - {{modules}} modules × 3 servos, 1 feeder, {{irSensors}} IR sensors, {{channelsUsed}} of the PCA9685's 16 channels in use. The remaining channels are free for additional sorting modules (up to 5 modules on a single PCA9685). Check off each part as you gather it - checkmarks are saved in this browser.
bom.affiliateDisclaimer: Some "Buy" links are Amazon affiliate links - we may earn a small commission on qualifying purchases at no extra cost to you.
bom.hopperNote: There are two hopper styles: the classic hopper and a newer design that accommodates different card thicknesses more easily. Parts tagged Optional, classic hopper or Optional, new hopper below belong to whichever style you aren't building - you only need one set.

unoR4.notes: Runs {{path}}; USB connection to the host computer for Web Serial

esp32.notes: Runs {{path}}; USB connection to the host computer for Web Serial - also flashable straight from the app afterward, see /app once it's set up

esp32Wroom.notes: Runs {{path}}; USB connection to the host computer for Web Serial. Update its firmware via the Arduino IDE only - the in-app browser flasher targets the ESP32-S3 build specifically and isn't safe to use on this board.

pca9685.notes: I²C servo driver - drives all 10 servos

sg90Positional.notes: 3 per module × {{count}} modules - bottom trapdoor, paddle gate, pusher

sg90Continuous.notes: Feeder - drives cards out of the hopper into module 1

irSensor.notes: One at the gate of each module (1-{{count}}), plus one in the hopper throat

psu.notes: Dedicated servo bus power into the PCA9685 V+ terminal - do not power 10 servos off the {{board}}'s onboard 5V. 5.5mm x 2.5mm barrel plug, center positive.

usbCableEsp32.notes: ESP32-S3 dev board ↔ host computer, via the board's native USB port

usbCableEsp32Wroom.part: USB-A–to–USB-C or Micro-USB cable (check which port your specific board has)
usbCableEsp32Wroom.notes: ESP32-WROOM-32 dev board ↔ host computer, via its USB-to-serial bridge chip (CP2102/CH340, depending on the board) - the connector itself is USB-C on newer boards, Micro-USB on older ones

barrelJack.part: DC barrel jack or screw-terminal pigtail
barrelJack.notes: Adapts the PSU output to the PCA9685's V+ / GND terminal

enclosure.notes: Print from <mesh>card_sorter.3mf</mesh> (mesh, slicer-ready) or <source>Card Sorter.f3d</source> (Fusion 360 source)

filament.notes: Quantity per your slicer's estimate for the model above

oRing.notes: Fitted onto the feeder roller for grip on the card face

hopperORing.notes: New hopper style - accommodates different card thicknesses more easily than the classic hopper

binHolders.notes: 2 per module ({{count}} modules) - one left, one right - catches the cards the pusher ejects to each side

m3x6Screw.notes: 14 attach each bin base to the housing; 8 attach the base panels to the base; 2 mount a camera or phone bracket

m3Nut.notes: Paired with the base panel M3×6 screws

m3x10Screw.notes: Attaches the variable-height wall to the hopper tube

m3Washer.notes: Used with the M3×10 screws on the classic hopper's variable-height wall, or with the new hopper's fasteners - needed either way

hopperSpring.notes: New hopper style - tensions the adjustable wall against the card stack

m2x6Screw.partSpec: (20 for 2 modules, +6 per module beyond that, +7 for the board mount, +1 per IR sensor)
m2x6Screw.notes: 20 for 2 modules, +6 per additional module ({{count}} modules): flapper (bottom/sides) and pusher arms; +7 to mount the {{board}} and PCA9685 servo driver board to the base panels; +1 per IR sensor ({{irCount}} total)

servoHornScrew.notes: Included with each servo; secures the horn to the shaft

hookupWire.notes: IR sensor/Servos. Using these you may have to daisy chain some together, just electrical tape them to make sure they don't come apart.

wagoConnectors.notes: Splices power and ground to each IR sensor without twisting/soldering wires together

dupontConnectors.notes: These are only needed if you're making your own custom length wires.

dupontCrimper.notes: These are only needed if you're making your own custom length wires.

webcam.notes: This is the one I use - any webcam works as long as you can manually adjust focus, brightness, etc. (auto-adjusting can throw off scans)

cameraMountScrew.notes: Standard tripod-mount thread - screws into a webcam or phone mount's socket

wiring.heading: Wiring
wiring.description: Everything hangs off one I²C bus (PCA9685) and {{count}} digital input pins (IR sensors). The PCA9685's logic side runs off the {{board}}'s onboard supply; its <pin>V+</pin> servo rail must come from the external supply, and that supply's ground must be tied back to the {{board}}'s ground - a floating servo ground is the most common reason a freshly wired unit won't move.

i2c.title: I²C bus
i2c.esp32Note: Wire PCA9685 VCC to the ESP32's 3.3V pin, not 5V - the I²C pull-ups follow whatever powers the PCA9685, and feeding 5V into an ESP32 GPIO can damage it. The PCA9685 chip itself runs its logic fine at 3.3V, so this costs nothing.

diagram.title: Wiring diagram
diagram.alt: Wiring diagram showing the PCA9685, microcontroller, servo, and IR sensor connections
diagram.esp32Note: This diagram shows the Arduino wiring for reference - the connection layout is the same on ESP32 (PCA9685 over I²C, one IR sensor per digital pin), just use the pin numbers and 3.3V logic voltage from the tables above instead of what's pictured.

irSensors.description: All {{count}} read active-LOW (pin goes low when a card is present) using the {{board}}'s internal pull-up - wire the sensor's digital OUT straight to the pin, no external pull-up resistor needed.
irSensors.esp32Note: Power these sensors' VCC from the ESP32's 3.3V pin if the module supports it, not 5V - their digital OUT tends to swing up to whatever VCC they're fed, and 5V on OUT risks damaging the GPIO it's wired to. Check your specific sensor's datasheet accepts 3.3V.

channelMap.unused: Unused - available for additional sorting modules

assembly.heading: Assembly
assembly.description: Eight phases, structural work first. Checkboxes are saved in this browser, so you can close the tab mid-build and pick back up later.
assembly.helpText: Stuck on a step? Join the Discord if you need help.

printSortingModule.text: Slice and print {{count}} Sorting Module plates - one per sorting module - from <mesh>card_sorter.3mf</mesh> (or re-export from <source>Card Sorter.f3d</source>).

printFeederModule.text: Print 1 Feeder Module from the same file - only one needed, regardless of module count. Houses the feeder roller and hopper throat.

printSortingModuleShroud.text: Print 1 Sorting Module Shroud - only one needed. The cover that sits over the stacked modules.

printPlateBase.text: For {{modules}} sorting modules, print {{count}} Base Support pieces from the same file - the modules stack in a staircase, so each added tier needs one more support piece than the tier above it. Change the module count in the parts list above to update this.

printGenericBase.text: For {{modules}} sorting modules, print {{count}} Generic Plates. Change the module count in the parts list above to update this.

printBinHolders.text: For {{modules}} sorting modules, print {{count}} bin holders - two per module, one for the left ejection side and one for the right. Change the module count in the parts list above to update this.

dryFit.text: Dry-fit each module housing before inserting any electronics - sand or adjust any tight servo pockets now.

mountBoardsToPanels.text: Mount the {{board}} and PCA9685 servo driver board to the base panels with 7 M2×6 screws.

attachBasePanels.text: Attach the base panels to the base with 8 M3×6 screws and 8 M3 nuts.
attachBasePanels.note: Do this after the {{board}} and PCA9685 are mounted to the panels - the boards are much harder to reach once the panels are on the base.

installEsp32Core.text: In the Arduino IDE, add the ESP32 board index URL (File → Preferences → Additional boards manager URLs): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/gh-pages/package_esp32_index.json, then install "esp32 by Espressif Systems" from the Boards Manager.
installEsp32Core.note: This pulls down a few hundred MB (the whole Xtensa toolchain) and takes a few minutes.

installLibraries.text: In the Arduino IDE, install the ArduinoJson and Adafruit PWM Servo Driver libraries.
installLibraries.note: Library Manager → search each by name.

uploadSketch.text: Select board "Arduino Uno R4", select the correct port, then upload firmware/main/main.ino.

uploadSketchEsp32.text: Select board "ESP32S3 Dev Module", set Tools → USB Mode to "Hardware CDC and JTAG" and USB CDC On Boot to "Enabled", select the correct port, then upload firmware/main/main.ino.
uploadSketchEsp32.note: Uses the ESP32-S3 pin layout already in the sketch (see the IR_PINS comment in main.ino) - building on a classic ESP32 WROOM board instead? Switch to that board option above, its own pin layout is already in the sketch too. Hardware CDC/JTAG mode with CDC On Boot enabled is required for the board to show up on its native USB port at all, and it's what lets the in-app browser flasher reset the board into bootloader mode reliably without a BOOT-button press; the tradeoff is the board enumerates under a generic Espressif name instead of "Mault Card Sorter".

uploadSketchEsp32Wroom.text: Select board "ESP32 Dev Module", select the correct port, then upload firmware/main/main.ino.
uploadSketchEsp32Wroom.note: Uses the classic-ESP32 pin layout already in the sketch (see the IR_PINS comment in main.ino) - no renumbering needed. Don't use the in-app browser flasher to update this board later: it fetches a binary built for the ESP32-S3 specifically, and writing that to a different ESP32 chip won't work correctly. Re-upload from the Arduino IDE instead whenever the firmware changes.

confirmReady.text: Open the Serial Monitor at 9600 baud and confirm you see {"status":"ready"} after the board resets.

mountModuleServos.text: Install the bottom, paddle, and pusher servo - all 180° positional SG90s - into each of the 3 module housings (9 servos total).
mountModuleServos.note: Don't install the horns onto the servo shafts yet - fit the flappers/pusher arm to their horns below, but leave the horn itself off the servo until each module is calibrated from the app.

centerServos.text: Wire all {{count}} module servos into their PCA9685 channels, plus the I²C bus and external servo power (see Wiring below). Then open /app/calibrate and click Connect - the app pushes each module's calibration and centers every servo automatically. Don't install any horn onto a servo shaft until it finishes.
centerServos.note: Not calibrated yet? It centers using sensible defaults instead. Safe to reconnect any time you need to re-center a servo before fitting or repositioning a horn.

mountBottomFlapper.text: Assemble the bottom paddle by screwing the paddle to the linkage, then the linkage to the horn. Remember not to install the horn to the servo yet.
mountBottomFlapper.note: This is the trapdoor a card falls through to reach the next module, or the current one on a match. The horn gets seated onto the servo once the module is calibrated from the app - see Calibrate from the app below.

mountSideFlappers.text: Assemble the side paddles by screwing the left and right flapper to the shared linkage, then the linkage to the horn (one pair per module). Remember not to install the horn to the servo yet.
mountSideFlappers.note: One paddle servo drives both flappers together - they open and close as a pair, not independently. The horn gets seated onto the servo once the module is calibrated from the app - see Calibrate from the app below.

mountPusherArm.text: Assemble the pusher by screwing the pusher arm to the linkage, then the linkage to the horn. Remember not to install the horn to the servo yet.
mountPusherArm.note: The horn gets seated onto the servo once the module is calibrated from the app - see Calibrate from the app below.

fitFeederOrings.text: Fit 6 G20 o-rings onto the feeder roller.
fitFeederOrings.note: These give the roller grip on the card face - space them evenly along the roller's length.

mountFeederRoller.text: Attach the roller to the feeder module.

mountFeederServo.text: Install the continuous-rotation feeder servo to the roller, at the base of the hopper.

mountFeederWall.text: Attach the wall piece to the hopper using the 2 M3×10 screws and M3 washers - it guides cards from the hopper to the feeder roller.
mountFeederWall.note: When mounting the wall, attach it to the feeder module first, then put 2 cards below the wall and slide it down before tighting it into place.

fitHopperRollerOrings.text: Fit o-rings onto the hopper roller.
fitHopperRollerOrings.note: Same as the feeder roller - these give it grip on the card face.

mountHopperRoller.text: Install the hopper roller into place on the hopper with 2 M3×8 screws and 2 M3 washers.

calibrateHopperRoller.text: Fit the spring and M3×25 screw, then use the screw to calibrate the wall so it lets only 1 card through at a time.
calibrateHopperRoller.note: Tighten the roller until it no longer free-spins, but can still be turned by hand.

mountModuleIr.text: Fix one IR sensor at the gate of each module (1-{{modules}}) with 1 M2×6 screw each, aimed across the card path.

mountHopperIr.text: Fix the remaining IR sensor in the hopper throat, just above the feeder, with 1 M2×6 screw.
mountHopperIr.note: This one tells the feeder when the hopper is empty - placement matters more than the module sensors.

wireI2c.text: Wire the PCA9685 to the {{board}}'s I²C bus (SDA/SCL) and logic power/GND.
wireI2c.note: See the Wiring section above - the logic voltage is 3.3V on ESP32, not 5V.

wireServos.text: Wire all {{count}} servos into PCA9685 channels 0–{{lastChannel}} and 15 per the channel map - the feeder always takes the last channel.
wireServos.note: There are wire channels, that use zip ties, in the side of the base to help keep everything neat.

wireSensors.text: Wire the {{count}} IR sensors to the digital pins listed in the Wiring section above - module gates and the hopper throat sensor don't all fall on consecutive pins.
wireSensors.note: For the power and ground, you will have to combine {{count}} wires into one, either with a breadboard or by twisting and soldering them together. You will need to manually calibrate the sensors to have a shorter throw, as to not get false positives.

wirePower.text: Bring the external 6V supply into the PCA9685 V+/GND terminal, and tie its ground to the {{board}}'s ground.
wirePower.note: Skipping the common ground is the #1 cause of servos that twitch but never move correctly.

connectSerial.text: Connect the {{board}} to the app via Web Serial, then open /app/calibrate.

calibrateModules.text: Module Calibration Grid - set the open/closed pulse for each bottom and paddle, and left/neutral/right for each pusher, module by module.

installHorns.text: Using the calibration grid above, put each paddle in its open position and each pusher in its neutral position, then press the horn (with its flapper or pusher arm already fitted) onto the servo shaft and secure it with the horn screw - bottom flapper, paddle flappers, and pusher arm, for all {{count}} module servos.
installHorns.note: Fitting a horn off-center biases the whole linkage - the exact open/closed and left/right pulses get fine-tuned afterward from the Module Calibration Grid above.

calibrateFeeder.text: Feeder Calibration Panel - tune feed speed, pulse/pause timing, and settle duration against your actual hopper.

checkIr.text: IR Sensor Panel - verify all {{count}} sensors report present/absent correctly with a card in hand.
checkIr.note: If a sensor doesn't trigger, or triggers with nothing in front of it, calibrate its detection distance manually: on the back of the sensor is a small blue box with a gray potentiometer dial. Turn it all the way one way so it detects nothing, then turn it slowly back until it just detects a card an inch or two in front of it.

testBins.text: Bin Routing Controls - send a test card to each of the 7 bins in turn and confirm it lands correctly.

runTestCommand.text: With the external servo supply connected, send {"test": true} over serial.
runTestCommand.note: Cycles every bottom and paddle open, sweeps all pushers left then right, resets to neutral, then briefly spins the feeder.

watchModules.text: Watch each module during the test - confirm nothing binds or grinds at the end of its travel.
watchModules.note: If a servo strains at open or closed, its housing cutout likely needs adjusting before calibration.

loadHopper.text: Load the hopper and confirm the feeder stops pulsing once the hopper IR reads empty.

fullPass.text: Run a full scan-to-bin pass end to end before leaving the unit unattended.
